Enhancement: Establish a current baseline that includes both the default Studio and workbench, with source, WASM, assets, browser, quality, and seed identities. Preserve the old frozen tournament as historical evidence.
Acceptance target: Reproduce each baseline from its manifest; distinguish cold/warm, active/settled, and current/historical results.

Enhancement: Instrument CPU stepping, snapshots, geometry staging, command encoding, and feature-gated GPU pass timestamps. Use a nonblocking ring of query/readback buffers.
Acceptance target: Attribute p50/p95/p99 costs by stage; unsupported timestamps display unavailable; no per-frame GPU wait.

Enhancement: Build capacity sweeps for active rigids, cloth nodes, water cells, contacts, material constraints, transparent instances, and recording duration.
Acceptance target: Record the largest passing workload at fixed quality/error and 16.67 ms p95 / 25 ms p99 interactive targets; derive `N0` from evidence.

Enhancement: Extend the benchmark gate to current Studio and complete frame workloads using isolated runs, balanced baseline/candidate order, and an unchanged control population.
Acceptance target: Reject material regressions using predeclared thresholds and confidence intervals; preserve raw samples and source identities.

Enhancement: Add numerical acceptance suites beyond finite-state/hash tests: constraint residuals, penetration, momentum, mass, strain, energy/work, and failure sequence. First reconcile the plate plasticity assertion that failed after the concurrent press changes.
Acceptance target: Each solver has a declared error envelope and long-horizon/action stress cases; exact optimizations retain exact reference output; intended press behavior and tests agree.

Enhancement: Introduce a shared engine/model adapter for Studio and workbench, covering commands, stepping, topology versions, state, and telemetry. Preserve each model's identity during migration.
Acceptance target: Run one model headlessly and in both shells with identical fixed-step commands and outputs; no UI-dependent physics behavior.

Enhancement: Replace scattered backend assumptions with one capability registry: model/solver ID, JS/scalar/SIMD/threaded/GPU mode, render backend, limits, and guarantees. Extend existing badges and diagnostics.
Acceptance target: Every run/export records the actual selected capabilities; unsupported combinations fail or select an explicitly identified fallback.

Enhancement: Expose a headless `create → command → step → inspect → destroy` runtime API instead of relying on DOM-driven orchestration for experiments.
Acceptance target: The same command file runs in a Node/browser worker harness and interactive shell; every instance releases owned resources.

Enhancement: Compile native and preview scenes from a common versioned recipe representation instead of maintaining parallel procedural family staging.
Acceptance target: Compare shapes, transforms, materials, and actions for all 800 recipes and 65 hero definitions; record intentional backend differences.

Enhancement: Give engineering recording a telemetry-only path. `recordEngineeringFixedStep()` currently calls `soft.buildFrame(false)` and native hashing on every recorded tick.
Acceptance target: Record the required 60 Hz channels without building render geometry per tick; at most one presentation build per displayed state; preserve evidence semantics.

Enhancement: Move fixed-step native/soft/Studio stepping into a dedicated worker behind the shared contract. Keep command order and model time authoritative there.
Acceptance target: UI remains responsive during a deliberately overloaded simulation; command-to-visible-state latency is measured; same-backend replay still passes.

Enhancement: Add a reusable transferable snapshot pool with ownership states and backpressure for deployments without shared memory.
Acceptance target: No detached-buffer reuse or unbounded message queue; measure transport overhead against the current direct path.

Enhancement: Add an optional SharedArrayBuffer snapshot ring with atomic publication and scene generations, gated by cross-origin isolation.
Acceptance target: No torn snapshot reads under stress; compatibility path still works; transfer cost falls without blocking the browser thread.

Enhancement: Interpolate presentation between timestamped physics snapshots, including quaternion rotation and discontinuity handling.
Acceptance target: Smooth 60/120/144 Hz display against fixed stepping; reset, teleport, and fracture never interpolate across incompatible topology.

Enhancement: Formalize accumulator overload behavior and wire the existing governor into presentation decisions. Current loops cap per-frame step count but retain backlog.
Acceptance target: Overload and dropped wall time are visible; no growing catch-up spiral; scientific recording pauses or reports lag instead of silently skipping simulation ticks.

Enhancement: Convert the Studio's object-per-particle/link solver to stable typed arrays, using the legacy soft kernels' data layout experience. Preserve traversal and arithmetic order first.
Acceptance target: Lower stepping CPU time and allocation rate for all three studies; exact same-version service/failure regression outputs before numerical redesign.

Enhancement: Add `snapshotInto()` or equivalent reusable live snapshot storage; allocate immutable copies only at recording/checkpoint boundaries.
Acceptance target: Zero new large typed buffers per live frame after warmup; saved frames remain immutable; compare against the 19–21 KB canopy/plate snapshot allocations.

Enhancement: Rebuild and upload Studio surface index buffers only when topology changes. Reuse precomputed border connectivity and explicit replay topology identities.
Acceptance target: No index upload on intact motion; torn faces remain absent; backward scrubbing reconstructs the correct topology.

Enhancement: Remove per-node temporary position arrays, temporary color objects, and repeated perimeter-pair construction from `StudioWorld.update()`.
Acceptance target: Allocation profiling shows stable hot-path storage; visual transforms/colors and severed-link visibility match the reference.

Enhancement: Replace snapshot-history splicing with a bounded ring plus asynchronously persisted chunks, retaining compact chart samples separately from full geometry snapshots.
Acceptance target: Long recordings remain within a configured memory budget; sample timestamps stay ordered; timeline seeking works across persisted chunk boundaries.

Enhancement: Connect Box3D's task scheduling to a bounded Emscripten pthread pool instead of `workerCount = 1`; implement task callbacks and a separately selected threaded artifact.
Acceptance target: Benchmark 1/2/4/8 workers on contact-heavy scenes, including startup/transport; prove deterministic guarantees per supported mode and retain single-thread deployment.

Enhancement: Replace the native bridge's fixed 4,096-body arrays and renderer cap with bounded, growable capacity tiers and explicit allocation-failure reporting.
Acceptance target: Exercise 4K/16K/64K active-body staging without truncation or stale heap views; publish actual contact-heavy frame times and memory use.

Enhancement: Add body destruction, slot reuse, and generation-checked handles for projectiles, debris, and streamed scenes.
Acceptance target: A million spawn/despawn operations maintain bounded live storage; stale IDs never mutate newly recycled bodies.

Enhancement: Export position, quaternion, and scale instead of full 4×4 rigid matrices; reconstruct transforms in shaders. Prototype a 40-byte float32 record before considering lossy packing.
Acceptance target: Reduce dynamic transform payload from 64 to 40 bytes/body; validate reconstructed positions/normals and benchmark total CPU/upload/GPU cost.

Enhancement: Evaluate coarse block dirty ranges for mixed sleeping/awake transform uploads, with a dense-upload threshold. This differs from the previously rejected sparse move-event synchronization.
Acceptance target: Win on defined large mixed-activity workloads without regressing dense scenes; include range detection and write-call overhead in timing.

Enhancement: Replace native global world state with explicit world contexts and per-world buffers, seeds, handles, and lifetimes.
Acceptance target: Multiple independent simulations can run/reset without cross-contamination; destruction and replay remain isolated.

Enhancement: Expose sphere, capsule, convex, mesh, compound, and heightfield geometry through the bridge and render the matching shape instead of only cube-hull instances.
Acceptance target: Query, collision, inertia, and visible geometry agree on a shape-parity suite; qualify support against the pinned upstream version.

Enhancement: Expose supported native joints, limits, motors, and kinematic targets through typed commands and diagnostics.
Acceptance target: Pendulum, slider, actuator, and driven mechanism tests meet declared limit/constraint errors; revise sleeping early-outs for kinematic/motor activity.

Enhancement: Add batched ray/shape casts, overlaps, contact events, and contact-impulse streams to the C ABI, with stable body/shape IDs.
Acceptance target: Contact/query results support picking and coupling without per-contact JS/WASM calls; report overflow and retain deterministically ordered events.

Enhancement: Qualify collision layers and per-body continuous-collision policies for authored scene classes. Sleep and CCD already exist; tune eligibility rather than adding them again.
Acceptance target: Reduce unnecessary pair/CCD work while thin-wall, high-speed, sensor, and wake-up regression cases remain correct.

Enhancement: Introduce compliant XPBD constraints where cloth/rope/Studio still rely on iteration-dependent PBD stiffness. Reuse the material shell's existing compliance concepts where appropriate.
Acceptance target: Calibrated extension/bending response stays within a declared tolerance across timestep and iteration sweeps; record constraint-force estimates.

Enhancement: Extend existing qualified adaptive schedules with residual-based convergence and explicit contact/damage escalation rules.
Acceptance target: Lower solver work at the same residual/error target; preserve conservative tearing/contact modes and long-horizon qualification.

Enhancement: Add a hierarchical constraint solve for large membranes, using coarse-to-fine corrections to address long-range stretch.
Acceptance target: At equal strain/shape error, outperform the flat solver on increasing grid sizes; measure topology-change maintenance cost.

Enhancement: Add cloth self-collision using a spatial hash or BVH over nonadjacent surface elements and a thickness-aware narrow phase.
Acceptance target: Folded and layered cloth avoids persistent interpenetration; neighbor-search cost scales acceptably on dense and adversarial folds.

Enhancement: Replace isolated ground/sphere collision assumptions with frictional cloth/rope contact against shared rigid collider geometry.
Acceptance target: Drape/slide/stack tests work on moving convex and mesh fixtures; contact thickness and friction are measurable.

Enhancement: Extend swept collision to fast soft vertices/edges and moving rigid shapes, beyond the existing projectile-specific interactions.
Acceptance target: High-speed thin-surface tests pass over a declared velocity range; time-of-impact/subdivision cost is included in budgets.

Enhancement: Add a physically parameterized cloth shell model with separate membrane stretch, shear, and bending, including directional fabric response.
Acceptance target: Warp/weft/bias and cantilever tests converge with resolution; old normalized cloth recipes keep their original model version.

Enhancement: Add orientation degrees of freedom and twist/bend constraints to cables using a Cosserat-rod model.
Acceptance target: Torsion, buckling, and clamped-twist examples match reference behavior; simple rope mode remains available for cheaper scenes.

Enhancement: Maintain compact active-constraint lists for torn Studio/soft systems, with stable external IDs and deterministic compaction at topology boundaries.
Acceptance target: Fully broken members incur no recurring projection work; failure order and diagnostics remain reproducible after compaction.

Enhancement: Add optional adaptive simulation resolution near strain, contact, and crack fronts, with conservative state transfer and a separately identified solver mode.
Acceptance target: Refinement/coarsening preserves mass, momentum, anchors, and accepted response; cost falls on localized-load cases without changing render-only LOD semantics.

Enhancement: Port the existing water field update to WebGPU compute ping-pong buffers, starting with the same equations and boundary conditions.
Acceptance target: Beat CPU plus upload at the measured crossover size; report mass/wave/phase error and complete render-inclusive time.

Enhancement: Port cloth integration and projection to compute using graph-colored Gauss-Seidel or qualified Jacobi batches.
Acceptance target: No concurrent writes to a shared position within a color pass; compare equal residual quality, dispatch overhead, collisions, and long-run drift.

Enhancement: Move rope constraint solving to compute, extending the existing rope presentation path rather than confusing expansion with numerical simulation.
Acceptance target: Large rope nets run from GPU state without CPU matrix staging or per-step readback; break/collision/load tests pass.

Enhancement: Prototype GPU material projection and damage evaluation after the CPU material reference and tolerance suite are stable.
Acceptance target: Match declared plastic-response and failure-event envelopes; record reduction-order/numerical differences; show whole-workload gain on large lattices.

Enhancement: Extend frame contracts with GPU buffer ownership, offsets, counts, versions, and backend lifetimes, so GPU solvers feed rendering directly.
Acceptance target: No mandatory full-state CPU readback in an ordinary GPU simulation frame; CPU and GPU producers remain explicitly distinguishable.

Enhancement: Keep tearing topology on GPU using stable face/edge IDs, active masks, scans, and generated index counts.
Acceptance target: Holes and detached regions remain correct without falling back to full CPU surface packing; deterministic-reference comparison accounts for event ordering.

Enhancement: Compute deformation normals, strain colors, and bounds once per changed state for shared presentation, including the Studio's CPU-normal path.
Acceptance target: Remove repeated CPU normal reconstruction; benchmark compute versus current vertex reconstruction at several mesh sizes; unchanged states do no work.

Enhancement: Move secondary spray, foam particles, dust, and visual debris to GPU spawn/update/compaction passes with bounded pools.
Acceptance target: Sustain a declared active-particle target without CPU object growth; presentation randomness cannot change authoritative physics replay.

Enhancement: Tune workgroup sizes, shared-memory tiles, and optional subgroup reductions by adapter class. Evaluate f16 only for qualified presentation/auxiliary data first.
Acceptance target: Record per-adapter winners and fallback paths; include small workloads; reject numerical or whole-frame regressions despite microkernel wins.

Enhancement: Reduce GPU telemetry to requested scalars/events and read it back through a bounded asynchronous staging ring, with timestamps and age tracking.
Acceptance target: Display and recording never block each frame on `mapAsync`/queue completion; delayed channels retain correct simulation timestamps and declared latency.

Category: 51–60: Two-way coupling and useful fluid simulation
Enhancement: Introduce a shared collider/interaction registry with stable IDs and one owner per projectile, fixture, or payload. Replace duplicated cross-domain action proxies incrementally.
Acceptance target: One physical projectile produces one contact history across rigid/soft domains; no duplicated mass or double-applied impulse.

Category: 51–60: Two-way coupling and useful fluid simulation
Enhancement: Add a staged coupling solve that exchanges soft contact and attachment reactions with Box3D instead of only broadcasting actions to both systems.
Acceptance target: Equal/opposite impulse accounting and bounded energy error in two-body/contact tests; strong-coupling cases remain stable under timestep refinement.

Category: 51–60: Two-way coupling and useful fluid simulation
Enhancement: Support moving rigid attachments, pulleys, and winch length control for ropes through the shared joint/coupling interface.
Acceptance target: A crane payload loads the hoist and support body; winch work, tension, and motor limits are observable rather than visual-only motion.

Category: 51–60: Two-way coupling and useful fluid simulation
Enhancement: Couple water buoyancy and drag to actual rigid hulls and return displaced volume/momentum to the field. Extend existing floater proxies.
Acceptance target: A floating body changes the water and vice versa; static float height and drag tests meet declared tolerances with stable force feedback.

Category: 51–60: Two-way coupling and useful fluid simulation
Enhancement: Add water bathymetry and obstacle masks to replace a uniform basin assumption, with boundary conditions derived from terrain and moving obstacles.
Acceptance target: A variable-depth lake-at-rest remains still within tolerance; channels, piers, and shore boundaries redirect flow correctly.

Category: 51–60: Two-way coupling and useful fluid simulation
Enhancement: Add a separate nonlinear shallow-water mode with a well-balanced, positivity-preserving wetting/drying treatment. Preserve the current linear model for its intended cases.
Acceptance target: Pass dry-front, dam-break, still-lake, and mass-balance cases; enforce a declared CFL policy; report resolution/time convergence.

Category: 51–60: Two-way coupling and useful fluid simulation
Enhancement: Tile large water/deformable domains with halo exchange and scalable topology indexing; use chunk-local indices or uint32 instead of assuming every surface fits uint16.
Acceptance target: A million-cell target domain crosses tile boundaries without seams, lost flux, or index overflow; capacity and transfer costs are reported.

Category: 51–60: Two-way coupling and useful fluid simulation
Enhancement: Generalize the single active surface/frame into a collection of independently versioned cloth, water, and sheet surfaces with per-surface resource lifetimes.
Acceptance target: Render and step multiple flags, basins, and material specimens simultaneously; mutations on one surface do not force unrelated uploads.

Category: 51–60: Two-way coupling and useful fluid simulation
Enhancement: Prototype an optional volumetric particle-fluid mode for overturning splashes and free surfaces that the heightfield cannot represent. Start with a bounded PBF/SPH research scene.
Acceptance target: Demonstrate a genuinely volumetric case with measured density/mass error and collision quality; publish the much higher compute/memory cost.

Category: 51–60: Two-way coupling and useful fluid simulation
Enhancement: Drive Studio river displacement, flow, and foam from the actual water solver through a renderer adapter, while retaining the existing visual river as an explicit mode.
Acceptance target: A changed obstacle or physical disturbance alters both measured water state and the visible river; visual presets do not fabricate physical currents.

Enhancement: Add explicitly unit-bearing material parameters and a calibration workflow with measured source datasets, specimen geometry, and parameter validity ranges. Retain normalized presets separately.
Acceptance target: Fit and validate against distinct datasets; exports distinguish normalized and calibrated model versions and retain units/uncertainty/provenance.

Enhancement: Build a material convergence matrix over specimen mesh, timestep, solve slices, and loading rate, extending the existing deterministic 100-case material campaign.
Acceptance target: Load-deflection curves, residual dent, and failure onset converge within declared envelopes; altered solver resolution cannot silently change conclusions.

Enhancement: Port the TypeScript material projection/damage hot loops to scalar and SIMD WASM, keeping the TypeScript implementation as the reference.
Acceptance target: Demonstrate speedup on actual material workloads including state handoff; all 100 existing material cases and new load/strike cases pass.

Enhancement: Extend the material solver's existing active-distance-member filtering with connected-island scheduling and conservative inactivity detection for undamaged idle regions.
Acceptance target: Skip only regions with no changing load/contact/damage driver; wake neighboring regions correctly; fatigue/loading histories match the reference.

Enhancement: Add a physically parameterized elastoplastic material option with hardening and directional response, beyond normalized rest-length creep and threshold tuning.
Acceptance target: Uniaxial load/unload, cyclic hardening, and directional coupon results match declared constitutive references; new state is checkpointed.

Enhancement: Add fatigue accumulation tied to measured stress/strain cycles and material data, including cycle counting and model applicability ranges.
Acceptance target: Predict held-out cyclic tests within a reported uncertainty interval; distinguish accumulated normalized damage from a calibrated fatigue prediction.

Enhancement: Make cohesive fracture mesh-objective by relating energy release and damage evolution to element size and material fracture energy. Extend existing cohesive cells/crack fronts.
Acceptance target: Refined meshes do not arbitrarily change total fracture work or failure load; compare crack paths and energy balance across resolutions.

Enhancement: Promote detached material fragments from local ballistic/ground-contact proxies into native rigid bodies, using bounded hull generation and conserved launch state.
Acceptance target: Fragments collide with external bodies and each other; transferred mass, momentum, and body budgets are accounted for; stable IDs survive promotion.

Enhancement: Add material-surface self-contact and persistent contact against punches, fixtures, and detached regions, extending the current local contacts.
Acceptance target: Folded sheets and crushing fragments do not pass through each other; contact convergence and frictional work are measured.

Enhancement: Extend reinforced concrete from persistent bridging constraints to bond-slip and pullout behavior with measured reinforcement/concrete interface parameters.
Acceptance target: Rebar transfers load after cover loss with testable slip, anchorage, and pullout behavior; strain and interface work remain distinct channels.

Enhancement: Add spatial bounds and view-frustum culling to the legacy all-instance draw stream; use independent light-frustum eligibility for shadows.
Acceptance target: Offscreen instances stop consuming main-pass vertex work; camera-edge and offscreen-shadow-caster tests retain correct visibility.

Enhancement: Add conservative hierarchical-depth occlusion culling for sufficiently large opaque scenes after frustum culling.
Acceptance target: Urban/warehouse scenes reduce GPU work; camera cuts, moving occluders, and disocclusion show no visible popping; small scenes can bypass it.

Enhancement: Generate visible instance lists and indirect draw arguments on GPU, grouped by geometry/material class, with a direct-draw fallback.
Acceptance target: Rendering scales with visible batches without CPU count readback; no reliance on nonportable multi-draw or unsupported nonzero first-instance behavior.

Enhancement: Partition opaque and transparent instance ranges. The legacy transparent pass currently redraws `safeCount` whenever any stream contains transparency.
Acceptance target: The transparent draw visits only transparent instances; preserve depth/blending behavior and measure vertex/fragment reduction on mixed scenes.

Enhancement: Cache static shadow contributions and update dynamic casters separately; fit shadow coverage to the active experiment and invalidate on relevant light/scene changes.
Acceptance target: Static frames avoid redundant shadow rendering; moving geometry, camera-dependent bounds, and low sun remain correct across both renderers.

Enhancement: Add screen-error-based rendering LOD for general rigid geometry, distant rope thickness, debris, and decorative stage details. Keep the physics mesh independent.
Acceptance target: Increase visible scene capacity at a predeclared image-error limit; inspection views retain needed detail; physical results remain unchanged.

Enhancement: Use measured GPU/frame cost to adjust render resolution and selected effects with hysteresis. Extend the existing quality presets and unused governor.
Acceptance target: Meet the selected p95 budget without oscillation; exports/benchmark comparisons lock quality; simulation dt and material parameters remain unchanged.

Enhancement: A/B test a depth prepass and opaque front-to-back ordering for expensive, overdraw-heavy scenes. Enable only above a measured crossover.
Acceptance target: GPU savings exceed added geometry/encoding cost; test both sparse scenes and heavy material overlap.

Enhancement: Add tiled or clustered local-light assignment if many dynamic lights become a product requirement. Preserve the existing cheaper directional/environment-light path.
Acceptance target: Bound per-fragment light work in a 100-local-light stress scene; verify light-list overflow, specular response, and GPU cost.

Enhancement: Build a measurable post-processing resource graph with pooled transient targets and selectively downsampled bloom/AO, extending the existing HDR and Studio AO passes.
Acceptance target: Lower render-target bandwidth/peak bytes at accepted image quality; resizing and quality transitions recreate dependent bindings safely.

Category: 81–90: Assets, large worlds, and resource lifetime
Enhancement: Generalize the Studio's existing GLTF scenery loading into an asset pipeline that cooks render meshes, collision geometry, material bindings, units, and bounds for authored simulations.
Acceptance target: Import one asset consistently into both shells; visual geometry and collider scale agree; unsupported assets produce actionable diagnostics.

Category: 81–90: Assets, large worlds, and resource lifetime
Enhancement: Apply offline meshoptimizer/gltfpack-style indexing, cache/fetch optimization, and simplification to imported static assets, beyond runtime mesh merging already present.
Acceptance target: Smaller/faster assets pass silhouette, UV, normal, and material checks; measure parse/upload/render costs as well as download bytes.

Category: 81–90: Assets, large worlds, and resource lifetime
Enhancement: Extend compressed texture delivery to the Studio's PNG/WebP material library using KTX2/Basis and capability-aware targets, preserving the legacy direct ASTC/BC path.
Acceptance target: Compare transfer bytes, resident texture payload, transcode startup, and normal-map quality across supported devices; retain appropriate fallback formats.

Category: 81–90: Assets, large worlds, and resource lifetime
Enhancement: Stream texture/mesh detail by demand with cancellation and residency budgets, instead of letting every visited finish/asset remain permanently resident.
Acceptance target: Rapid scene changes cancel obsolete work; memory stays within a configured budget; required visible assets recover without broken bindings.

Category: 81–90: Assets, large worlds, and resource lifetime
Enhancement: Make Studio vegetation spatially clustered with camera-dependent density/LOD and conservative bounds. Extend current instanced/tiered woodland rather than adding generic instancing.
Acceptance target: Wide bridge views reduce hidden/distant vegetation work; nearby trees retain silhouette/shadow quality; no asset identity changes in evidence captures.

Category: 81–90: Assets, large worlds, and resource lifetime
Enhancement: Load and compile the active study's necessary assets first. Defer unrelated study finishes and optional environments; preserve existing asynchronous pipeline creation.
Acceptance target: Measure time to first interactive specimen under cold cache and slow transfer; no blank materials or shader stalls when deferred content becomes visible.

Category: 81–90: Assets, large worlds, and resource lifetime
Enhancement: Add complete resource-owner lifecycles for both renderers: device buffers, targets, materials, textures, controls, observers, workers, and async tasks. Extend existing partial disposal.
Acceptance target: Repeated create/switch/destroy cycles plateau in owned resource counts and allocated bytes; no callbacks touch disposed objects.

Category: 81–90: Assets, large worlds, and resource lifetime
Enhancement: Add explicit mid-session GPU device-loss recovery: preserve CPU state or the latest GPU checkpoint, reselect capabilities, recreate resources, and report recovery status.
Acceptance target: Deliberately lose the device during running, paused, recording, and resize states; recover a valid scene or a clear recoverable error.

Category: 81–90: Assets, large worlds, and resource lifetime
Enhancement: Add regional coordinates/floating origins and explicit world-to-local transforms for large engineering sites, including collider, camera, and recorder coordinates.
Acceptance target: Move scenes through large world coordinates while local contact/strain accuracy stays within tolerance; exports retain consistent world positions.

Category: 81–90: Assets, large worlds, and resource lifetime
Enhancement: Add a versioned, integrity-checked persistent asset cache and offline package manifest for repeat lab use; coordinate invalidation with native/shader revisions.
Acceptance target: Repeat/offline startup uses the correct cached release; mixed-version assets cannot silently load; cache quotas and recovery are tested.

Enhancement: Define renderer adapters over shared engine state and explicit quality/capability semantics for raw WebGPU, Three.js WebGPU, and the Studio's existing WebGL fallback.
Acceptance target: Renderer selection cannot silently change the physics model; missing render features are declared; the workbench's intentional WebGPU requirement stays explicit.

Enhancement: Split inline WGSL and the large renderer/coordinator modules into owned shader/pass/runtime modules, with interface layout checks and shader compilation coverage.
Acceptance target: Existing hardware shader validation still passes; WGSL/CPU layouts are checked together; no bundle/startup/per-frame regression from modularization.

Enhancement: Add authoring for parameterized fixtures, collider attachments, load programs, and model settings using the shared scene schema and reversible commands. Extend the existing presets/scene desk.
Acceptance target: An authored experiment round-trips with stable IDs and reproduces the same results; undo edits topology/settings without corrupting saved runs.

Enhancement: Extend existing run/evidence export into resumable checkpoints containing velocities/previous positions, damage, plastic rest state, RNG, constraints, and solver revision.
Acceptance target: Resume mid-failure and reproduce a continuous run under the same backend; reject incomplete or incompatible state rather than treating visual snapshots as full checkpoints.

Enhancement: Build cancellable parameter-sweep/batch execution on the headless runtime, with bounded concurrency and separate result artifacts.
Acceptance target: Sweep hundreds of cases without blocking the UI or overwriting benchmark evidence; report throughput, failures, cancellation, and per-case provenance.

Enhancement: Turn the existing remote TurboQuant experiment into an optional spectator/replay transport with sequence numbers, keyframes, error budgets, and loss recovery. Keep local transport uncompressed by default.
Acceptance target: Bandwidth savings survive encode/decode and loss/reorder tests; drift and end-to-end latency are measured; authoritative solver state is never overwritten by lossy presentation data.

Enhancement: Extend recorded/synthetic single-channel analysis into explicitly bound multi-channel solver/test measurements: synchronization, units, uncertainty, sensor locations, and provenance.
Acceptance target: Correlation/modal tools can distinguish measured inputs, solver outputs, and proxies; mismatched units or unknown channels cannot produce an unlabeled physical conclusion.

Enhancement: Add sensitivity analysis and bounded parameter fitting over batch experiments, including identifiability checks and held-out validation.
Acceptance target: Recover parameters in known synthetic cases and report uncertainty/held-out fit on measured cases; expose non-identifiable or model-mismatch results.

Enhancement: Expand current validation into a release matrix across both entry routes, target desktop/mobile GPUs, fallback modes, active/paused/replay states, and long thermal/memory runs.
Acceptance target: Store numerical, GPU-error, frame-time, and visual evidence separately; include interaction and second-camera checks; do not infer universal performance from a Node/Dawn pass.

Enhancement: Extend source/build provenance to current Studio, shaders, textures, and new native variants, with unique run directories and non-destructive default benchmark commands.
Acceptance target: Reproduce packaged artifacts and trace a report to exact inputs; ordinary validation cannot overwrite frozen evidence or consume another run's temporary build output.
